findings.message: D2 commits to applying the alias through “all resolution routes” without defining an existing authority, conservative over-approximation, or acknowledged implementation-depth bound for that open set. Record which permitted resolution is chosen so the obligation is bounded.

The permanent ADR cites the track-local `observations` artifact as evidence in Context. This reverse reference makes the ADR depend on a track-internal document; retain the historical fact without citing the downstream artifact.
D2 は「その他の解決経路」「すべての解決経路」が単一通過点を経由するという未限定の普遍的義務を決定しているが、対象経路の完全な範囲、既存権威への委譲、保守的過近似、または実装深度見積りのいずれも記録していない。将来経路まで含む実装範囲が収束しないため、採用する解決方針を Decision または Consequences に明記すべき。

D2 commits that every identity-universe consumer must pass through the same canonicalization stage, but it does not record a permitted resolution for this open-ended universal obligation (delegation, conservative over-approximation, or strict implementation with an acknowledged depth estimate). This leaves future consumers unbounded and the decision non-convergent.

D2 embeds implementation and test-structure prescriptions (the exact canonicalization placement, domain API visibility constraints, bypass-route handling, and verifying alias knowledge exists in exactly one code location). Removing these operational details would leave the architectural decision unchanged; they should be omitted or delegated to downstream specification/convention artifacts.

findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR
findings.message: D1 と D3 で、未実装かつ `module_path` 省略の add 型を表す決定が両立していません。D1 は catalogue 宣言から具体的な rustdoc summary を合成して解決集合へ入れる一方、D3 はこの場合の module を未確定のままにします。rustdoc summary の `[crate, name]` は crate root を表すため、D1 に従うと D3 が否定した root 扱いへ戻り、D3 に従うと D1 の summary を構成できません。未確定 module の identity を解決集合でどう保持するか、両決定を一つの方針に揃える必要があります。

D2 commits to an open-ended universal obligation by covering unenumerated resolution routes, but its parenthetical merely names both existing-authority delegation and conservative over-approximation without selecting which resolution governs. Record one explicit resolution (or a strict implementation with a depth estimate) in the decision or Consequences.
D2 は「全経路」「対象経路は列挙せず」という開集合の普遍的コミットメントを置いていますが、「既存権威への委譲と保守的過近似」と選択肢を並べるだけで、どの権威へ委譲するのか、どの過近似を採用するのかを確定していません。
Related の D7 引用は、参照先ADRの D7 が TypeKindV2 の entry struct 定義を扱っており、module_path 省略を crate root とする決定ではないため、本文の根拠関係と一致しません。
D1/D2 は対象経路を列挙せず、すべての参照解決経路を単一の取得口へ通すという開集合の義務を置いています。しかし括弧内は「既存権威への委譲」と「保守的過近似」を併記するだけで、委譲先の権威も過近似する集合も確定していません。許可された解決方法のいずれか一つを具体的に記録してください。
D2 は未列挙の将来の解決経路まで単一通過点へ通す開集合の義務を定めていますが、「既存権威への委譲」の委譲先として示す D1 の解決集合構築は ADR 内で新たに定める仕組みであり、許可された既存権威ではありません。実装範囲を収束させる許可済みの解決を明記してください。
D1 の「全経路」と D2 の列挙しない対象経路は普遍量化された義務だが、D2 が委譲先とする D1 の解決集合構築は経路集合を独立に確定する既存権威ではなく、同じ全経路通過義務を言い換えた循環的な委譲になっている。このままでは将来追加される解決経路までどう収束して捕捉するかが未解決である。既存の独立した権威・保守的過近似・深さ見積りを伴う厳密実装のいずれかを決定として記録する必要がある。

`TraitImplRequired` は `entry.module_path()` の `None` を `ModulePath::root()` に変換して `has_trait_impl` に渡しているため、配置未指定の型を crate root に誤認します。実装が `generated::Thing` にある場合、`Thing` への required trait impl が存在しても identity 不一致として欠落報告になります。省略 placement の action-aware 解決をこの経路にも適用してください。

標準外部 trait の identity seed を `FullyQualifiedItemPath::from_fully_qualified_key` で生成しており、これは互換 API として `PlacedType` を作ります。namespace discriminator 導入後も `core::fmt::Debug` 等が trait identity ではなく type identity として解決集合に入り、ドメインの type/trait namespace invariant を破っています。trait-specific constructor を使用すべきです。

The linter builds a combined universe containing distinct type and trait identities, but classifies every extracted path with the namespace-agnostic resolver. When a type and trait share a short name, type-only fields such as `handles` can now fail with `AmbiguousIdentifier` or resolve to the wrong local namespace, despite D3 requiring type/trait comparisons to remain separate. Carry the syntactic/expected namespace into classification and add a same-named type/trait linter regression test.

The rule-independent preflight inspects every TypeRef slot, including `trait_impl.trait_ref`, supertrait bounds, and generic bounds, but this newly added context hard-codes every extracted path to the Type namespace. Consequently two same-named traits referenced by a bare bound are filtered out as unresolved instead of producing the required fail-closed ambiguity; a same-named type can also be selected in their place. Namespace must be carried per extracted path occurrence (for example in `ExtractedTypeRefPath::Path`) or supplied accurately for each syntactic slot, with a trait-ambiguity regression test.

The fix carries one namespace for the entire `TypeRef`, not for each extracted path occurrence. A bound such as `Into<Result<alpha::Event, beta::Event>>` contains a trait path plus nested type paths, so passing `Trait` here makes the nested types appear unresolved and lets their ambiguity bypass preflight; conversely, a type slot such as `Box<dyn Port>` classifies `Port` as a type. Encode `CatalogueItemNamespace` on each `ExtractedTypeRefPath::Path` occurrence and add a mixed nested type/trait regression test.

Root-vs-nested semantics are inferred from the occurrence’s vector index, but `TypeRefPathExtractorPort::extract` does not require root-first ordering and `ExtractedTypeRefPath::Path` does not encode path position. A conforming adapter that emits a nested path first can therefore receive the slot namespace while the actual root remains classified as `Type`, suppressing a required trait ambiguity. Encode `Root`/`Nested` in each path occurrence (or make ordering an enforced contract) instead of using `index == 0`.

Root detection by spelling is still ambiguous when the root and a nested occurrence have the same path. For a trait slot such as `Foo<Foo>`, the parser emits both paths as type-position `Foo`; `root_path_is_anchored` returns true for both, so the nested type argument is incorrectly classified in the Trait namespace and a same-named type ambiguity is silently missed. Encode Root/Nested position on each extracted occurrence (or equivalent positional metadata) rather than deriving it from path text.
T001 の description は「baseline/current 候補規則」「baseline 一意性」「明示 path の完全一致」「曖昧時の fail-closed」という挙動契約を散文で再記述しています。対象・操作・anchor cite に限定してください（no-upstream-restatement policy）。
T002 の description は「add 相互参照」「modify→add」「宣言順序非依存」「未知参照拒否」などの上流挙動契約を再記述しています。
T003 の description は「四経路が同じ結果を使用し fail-closed を維持」という挙動契約を再記述しています。
T004 の description は bin target の type add/modify/reference、function path、一対一制約という上流契約を再記述しています。
T005 の description は完全修飾 key の記録、解決不能・曖昧 carrier の fail-closed という挙動契約を再記述しています。
section S1 の description は配置状態、namespace-aware 候補選択、明示・省略 path の fail-closed 挙動を再記述しています。対象・操作・anchor cite のみにしてください。
section S2 の description は解決集合の一箇所構築と crate-root alias の単一通過という上流設計を再記述しています。
section S3 の description は四経路の共通結果移行と route-local fallback 撤去という上流設計を再記述しています。
section S4 の description は function identity/catalog import の共通正準化と一対一 bin target の回帰挙動を再記述しています。
section S5 の description は trait-impl carrier の完全修飾 key 解決と短名 fallback 撤去を再記述しています。

T003 names the non-existent `libs/infrastructure/src/tddd/encoder.rs`; the codec encoder is `libs/infrastructure/src/tddd/catalogue_to_extended_crate_codec/encoder.rs`, with deletion handling in `encoder_deletions.rs`. The executor must therefore infer the load-bearing CO-01/AC-01/AC-03 write boundary. Name the actual target files explicitly.

T003 bundles independently verifiable migrations for the codec/deletion route (CO-01, AC-01, AC-03), type-signal identity index (CO-01, AC-01, AC-02), and Phase 1 definition-path authority (CO-01, AC-03). Because each route has its own target and regression surface, split them into separate pre-implementation tasks.

T004 bundles two independently verifiable consumers: function identity in `signal_evaluator_v2` and catalog import/bin-root resolution in `catalog_gen`/`schema_export` (IN-02, CO-02, AC-02). Split these behavior units so each can be implemented and validated independently.

B2 groups T003 and T004 despite a concrete overlapping test target: T003's Phase 1 validation and T004's function-identity validation both use `libs/infrastructure/src/tddd/signal_evaluator_v2/tests.rs`. This prevents isolated ownership within the batch; separate the tasks into different batches or assign disjoint test files explicitly.

After T002 runs in B1, T004, T006, and T007 are all ready and have write targets disjoint from T002's codec/canonical-identity files. Each individually fits B1's infrastructure ceiling: T004 gives 400+80=480, T006 gives 400+90=490, and T007 gives 400+70=470 (ceiling 500). Deferring all three to B2 is avoidable serialization; move at least one into B1 after T002.
T003、T006、T007、T008 はいずれも未着手で、依存先 T002 完了後に実行可能です。各タスクの production/test 対象は相互に重複せず、B1 に移しても infrastructure 合計は production 435 行・test 445 行で ceiling 500 未満です。しかし B2 に分離されており、不要なバッチ直列化が残っています。

Placed `add` declarations return before consulting the baseline. Consequently, a qualified key or explicit module path that exactly matches an existing baseline identity is accepted and encoded as `Add`, although D3 requires that collision to fail closed. Use the shared action-aware domain resolver for both placed and unplaced identities.

Serializing an unplaced identity omits its module segments, producing `[crate, name]`; `summary_identity` subsequently reconstructs that as a placed crate-root identity. Thus an unimplemented `add` with omitted `module_path` is emitted and resolved as crate-root rather than retaining D3's unplaced state.

Root-alias normalization is applied to every `Crate::paths` summary, including entries with nonzero `crate_id`. An external item whose crate name equals the binary rustdoc root is therefore rewritten into the catalogue package namespace and may resolve as a local type. Restrict alias rewriting to local summaries.

The renderer converts an omitted module path to `ModulePath::root()` before inserting the declaration into its identity index. Bare unplaced declarations therefore become concrete root identities and can receive edges as though their placement were known; the grouping and label paths make the same conversion. Preserve unplaced placement or resolve it from a qualified key instead of defaulting it to root.

For an `add` with omitted `module_path` and no baseline/current match, `identity_for_key` returns an `Unplaced*` identity, but `assign_local_entry` canonicalizes `fully_qualified.to_string()` (for example `domain::First`). The shared resolver intentionally does not match qualified paths to unplaced identities, so valid unimplemented adds such as the mutual `First`/`Second` case fail closed instead of being encoded. Use the original bare key when the identity is unplaced.

`encode_doc` still constructs baseline/current rustdoc paths from every catalogue declaration, including `Add` entries. The action-aware D3 resolver therefore sees each add as an existing baseline collision; 67 of the 101 codec tests currently fail before exercising their intended behavior. This also recreates the substitute resolution universe explicitly forbidden by T002. Keep only genuine baseline/current and external paths, letting production construction synthesize catalogue adds.

The signal-evaluator fixture independently injects all catalogue types and traits into both authoritative rustdoc inputs. Five of the 69 evaluator tests consequently fail in codec setup with `UnresolvedIdentifier` instead of reaching evaluation. Build scenario-accurate baseline/current crates and let the production resolution-set constructor supply add declarations.

The new qualified-baseline-collision regression test is itself red: the codec rejects the collision as `UnresolvedIdentifier("domain::generated::Thing")`, while the test and candidate-bearing collision contract require `AmbiguousIdentifier`. The final test suite cannot pass until the qualified collision preserves the intended typed diagnostic or the assertion is aligned with the approved contract.

Encoding maps both `None` and `Some(ModulePath::root())` to the same empty string, while decoding an empty string always produces `None`. A bare explicitly root-placed type or trait therefore round-trips as unplaced and is subsequently resolved under different D3 rules. Preserve the distinction between an omitted field and an explicitly empty root path in the DTO conversion.

The renderer classifies every entry with `module_path == None` as unplaced without considering that a qualified catalogue key itself supplies explicit placement. For example, `domain::alpha::Thing` with an omitted field is indexed as the placed `alpha` identity but rendered under `<unplaced>::Thing` outside the `alpha` module subgraph. Derive the effective placement from both key and optional field, as required by D3.

Unplaced catalogue additions are registered with `register_path`, which always emits `crate_id: 0`. This converts an unresolved/unplaced identity into a placed crate-root identity in the encoded `Crate::paths`; Phase 1 and downstream consumers then treat the add as `crate::Name` rather than an unplaced declaration, defeating the synthetic unplaced marker and corrupting identity reconciliation.

Unplaced catalogue additions are still registered through `register_path`, which always emits `crate_id: 0`. The encoded `Crate::paths` therefore presents an unresolved/unplaced addition as a placed crate-root identity; Phase 1 and downstream consumers can reconcile it as `crate::Name`, defeating the synthetic unplaced marker and changing identity semantics.

`merge_authoritative_paths` chooses `next_id` from baseline IDs only and does not reserve IDs already present in `current`. For example, with baseline IDs `{5, 10}` and current IDs `{11: A, 5: B}`, if ID 11 is visited first, remapping ID 5 subsequently overwrites `A` at ID 11. Because iteration order is unspecified, the shared resolution set can silently and nondeterministically lose an authoritative path. Allocate from the complete baseline/current ID union or probe for an unused ID before insertion.

`merge_definition_path_maps` recreates a route-local resolution map and allocates replacement IDs using only the baseline maximum. If a non-colliding catalogue entry already occupies `next_id`, a later colliding entry overwrites it, depending on `HashMap` iteration order. Phase 1 can therefore lose definition paths and misresolve impl identities. Consume the shared resolution set, or reserve/probe the complete ID union.

The Phase 1 remap classifies every nonzero `crate_id` as external. This includes `SYNTHETIC_UNPLACED_CRATE_ID`, which denotes a local add whose module is unresolved. Such additions are excluded from the local remap and mutual add references are redirected to fresh external IDs, while their placement marker is lost downstream. Treat the synthetic marker as local-unplaced and preserve it through S construction.

Phase 1 still builds a single path-string map for both types and traits. `build_type_trait_identity_map` keys entries only by `summary.path.join("::")`, so when the codec emits a type and trait with the same catalogue path, one ID is silently discarded and its action never reaches evaluation. Phase 1 must retain the namespace in its identity key or use separate type and trait maps.

`local_id_for_path` canonicalizes against the unfiltered type-and-trait universe and then uses the unfiltered local identity index. With a type and trait sharing a catalogue path, a valid type-position reference such as a field of type `Shared` becomes `AmbiguousIdentifier`. Thread the syntactic namespace into this lookup and use the corresponding namespace-filtered paths/index.

A trait impl's `for_type` is necessarily in the type namespace, but its canonicalization receives the complete type-and-trait resolution set. If a type and trait share the same path, type-signal indexing fails as ambiguous even though the owner is unambiguously the type. Canonicalize `for_type` using the type-only path set.

Phase 1 still collapses type and trait identities into the same `BTreeMap<String, Id>` keyed only by `summary.path.join("::")`. A catalogue/rustdoc input containing same-path entries in the two supported namespaces causes one identity to be silently discarded, so its action and references are omitted or misresolved. Preserve the namespace in the identity key or maintain separate maps.

After `merge_authoritative_paths` remaps a baseline/current ID collision above the input maximum, this resets `next_id` from the original input IDs rather than the merged map. For baseline IDs `{5,10}` and current IDs `{5,11}`, the merge allocates ID 12; the first catalogue-only `add` then also uses ID 12 and silently overwrites that authoritative current path. Seed synthetic allocation from the merged paths or use the same checked unused-ID allocator.

Namespace enforcement only applies when a path carries the unresolved/std marker. A path ID already assigned by the parser is returned unchanged, even if its item belongs to the opposite namespace; the added Type→Trait fallback also deliberately crosses namespaces. Consequently a type slot can bind to a trait, while a trait reference can bind to a same-named type. Revalidate every local ID against the requested namespace and remove the cross-namespace fallback.

Phase 1 still consumes `build_type_trait_identity_map`, whose key contains only the joined path and not `CatalogueItemNamespace`. The codec now permits a type and trait at the same catalogue path, but this map silently retains one ID, so the other declaration and its action never reach Phase 1. Use namespace-bearing keys or separate type and trait maps throughout Phase 1 state.

The production portion of this module is about 725 lines after excluding both `#[cfg(test)]` sections, exceeding the repository's 700-line production-module maximum. Move the newly added rustdoc canonicalization/definition-path merge helpers into a cohesive sibling module.

Phase 1 still collapses type and trait identities into one `BTreeMap<String, Id>` keyed only by `summary.path.join("::")`. With the namespace-aware catalogue now allowing same-path type and trait declarations, one entry is silently discarded by `or_insert`, so its action and references are omitted or misresolved. Preserve the namespace in the identity key or use separate maps.

`resolution_paths_for_catalogue` seeds synthetic-add allocation from the maximum input ID, but `merge_authoritative_paths` may already allocate a remapped current path above that maximum. A subsequent synthetic add can reuse the remapped ID and overwrite an authoritative path. Seed from the merged map or share the checked unused-ID allocator.

`local_id_for_path_with_legacy_trait_fallback` still resolves type-namespace paths against the trait namespace when type resolution fails. This permits a type-position reference to bind to a trait and violates namespace isolation; remove the cross-namespace fallback.

Phase 1 still uses the path-only `build_type_trait_identity_map` throughout its A/B identity processing. The new namespace-aware codec can produce type and trait declarations with the same path, but the map retains only one entry, silently dropping the other action from Phase 1.

The production portion of `phase1/builder/main_fn.rs` runs through line 732 (the test module starts at line 735), exceeding the repository’s 700-line production-module maximum. Move the newly added canonicalization and ID-merge helpers into a sibling module.

After `merge_authoritative_paths` remaps an ID collision, the merged map may contain an allocated ID above the original baseline/current maximum. `resolution_paths_for_catalogue` nevertheless seeds synthetic-add allocation from that original maximum, so the first catalogue-only add can reuse the remapped ID and overwrite an authoritative path. Seed from the merged map or use the checked unused-ID allocator.

`local_id_for_path_with_legacy_trait_fallback` still retries type-namespace resolution in the trait namespace, and already-assigned parser IDs bypass namespace validation entirely. A type-position reference can therefore bind to a trait or another wrong-namespace identity. Revalidate assigned local IDs against the requested namespace and remove the cross-namespace fallback.

The production portion of `phase1/builder/main_fn.rs` extends to approximately line 732 before the test module, exceeding the repository’s 700-line production-module maximum. Move the added canonicalization and definition-path merge helpers into a cohesive sibling module.

Type-alias spelling preservation changes namespace semantics. A `GenericBound::TraitBound` must resolve its root in the trait namespace, but the preserving route reuses a parser-assigned type namespace; the `~const` shortcut explicitly sets `Type`. Thus a valid local `~const LocalTrait` alias bound is rejected as a type lookup, while an alias bound naming a known local type can be encoded as a trait bound. Preserve the spelling only—always resolve bound roots as `Trait` and nested generic arguments as `Type`.

This production module is 713 lines and has no test-only section to exclude, exceeding the repository's 700-line production-module maximum. Move the new namespace-policy/state behavior or another cohesive responsibility into an existing sibling module.

The trait-root hint for `~const` bounds is applied only by `encode_bound_with_trait_root`, but trait declaration supertraits still call `encode_and_validate_bound` directly. That parser shortcut reaches this function with no pending hint, defaults the root to `Type`, and rejects a valid local declaration such as `trait Child: ~const LocalTrait`. Centralize the trait namespace in bound parsing or route every bound caller through the helper, with a supertrait regression test.

findings.category: missing AC coverage for a stated goal
findings.message: AC-03 does not specify D3's fail-closed result when an omitted-module_path `add` collides with a same-named baseline item. Its add cases all assume that the baseline name is absent, while CO-03 only rejects ambiguous or insufficiently grounded resolution; an existing baseline match is neither. An implementation that accepts this duplicate could therefore satisfy every stated AC, leaving GO-01's fail-closed module_path repair without deterministic acceptance coverage.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::identifiers::FullyQualifiedItemPath` cannot represent D3's unplaced add identity: its `module_path` remains mandatory (`ModulePath` and `&ModulePath`), while `from_catalogue_entry_key` accepts `Option<&ModulePath>`. The `None` case therefore has no valid `Self` representation, despite D3 requiring a crate/name identity with unresolved module placement.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::identifiers::FullyQualifiedItemPath` cannot represent D3's separate type/trait namespaces: both variants carry only crate/module/name, and `resolve_catalogue_identity` receives a single `BTreeSet<FullyQualifiedItemPath>` with no namespace discriminator. An unplaced add type and trait with the same name therefore collapse to one set element. Add namespace information to the identity universe so the required namespace-aware comparison is expressible.

CO-03/AC-03 has no declared enforcement owner. `domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::identity_resolution::resolve_catalogue_identity` receives neither `ItemAction` nor separate baseline/current sets, and `FullyQualifiedItemPath::from_catalogue_entry_key` likewise cannot apply the action-aware omission rules. The codec entry that does receive catalogue, baseline, and current data is not grounded to IN-03/CO-03/AC-03. Name exactly one capable owner for D3's fail-closed decisions and rejection data.

`usecase::CatalogPort` exposes filesystem-shaped operations (`items_dir: &Path`, implemented by `FsCatalogAdapter`) as an entirely synchronous port, but its docs do not acknowledge or justify the blocking choice. This prevents an I/O adapter from expressing async behavior through the port; document the deliberate sync boundary or correct the port color.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::identity_resolution::resolve_catalogue_identity` restates CO-01/CO-03 and AC-01/AC-03 by describing the single universe, fail-closed rejection, and absence of route-specific fallback. Replace the behavioral sentence with a concise target/purpose plus anchor cites, per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`CatalogueToExtendedCratePort` restates D1/IN-01 by saying catalogue encoding proceeds through the shared canonical identity-resolution set. Keep only the port purpose and anchor cites, per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`SignalEvaluatorPort` restates D2/IN-02 by specifying that its implementation consumes canonicalized type and function identities. Replace that behavioral clause with concise anchor cites, per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::entries::TraitEntry` restates CO-03/AC-03 by explaining that omitted `module_path` means unspecified rather than crate-root placement. Refer to the anchors without reproducing the rule, per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::entries::TypeEntry` restates CO-03/AC-03 by explaining that omitted `module_path` means unspecified rather than crate-root placement. Refer to the anchors without reproducing the rule, per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::identifiers::FullyQualifiedItemPath` restates D3's payload semantics and the rationale that omission must not be confused with crate root. Retain only the necessary type-shape description and anchor cites, per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`usecase::CatalogPort` restates IN-02/CO-02/AC-02 by describing the catalog-import delegation and canonicalization route. Replace that route behavior with a concise port purpose plus anchor cites, per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::identity_resolution::resolve_catalogue_identity_for_action` is grounded to D3 but carries no namespace, while `resolve_catalogue_identity_for_action_in_namespace` accepts `Option<CatalogueItemNamespace>`. For an unimplemented `add` with empty baseline/current sets, no candidate can reveal whether the identity is a type or trait; the `None` state therefore permits an add-trait request to become an unscoped/type identity instead of `UnplacedTrait`. Make the namespace required on the action-aware contract (or provide separate type/trait APIs) so this illegal state is unrepresentable.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::identity_resolution::resolve_catalogue_identity_for_action` and `resolve_catalogue_identity_for_action_in_namespace` are both `action: add` entries with identical parameter lists (including required `CatalogueItemNamespace`), return type, role, and spec grounding. They therefore declare two public names for the same action- and namespace-aware operation. Consolidate them into one contract instead of maintaining duplicate resolution surfaces.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::identity_resolution::resolve_catalogue_identity_for_action` is a namespace-agnostic action-aware contract even though D3 requires type/trait namespace separation. Its wrapper passes `None` to the namespaced resolver, whose unplaced-add path defaults `None` to `CatalogueItemNamespace::Type`; an add-trait request with no candidates can therefore be represented as `UnplacedType` rather than `UnplacedTrait`. Require the namespace or expose separate type/trait APIs so this illegal state is unrepresentable.

`domain::tddd::catalogue_v2::identity_resolution::resolve_catalogue_identity_for_action` is grounded to D3 but carries no namespace, and its companion `resolve_catalogue_identity_for_action_in_namespace` still permits `namespace: None`. AC-03 requires an empty-candidate `add` to produce either an unplaced type or unplaced trait identity, which cannot be selected without a required namespace. The namespace-agnostic/`None` state therefore leaves the action-aware contract unable to represent an unimplemented add trait correctly. Make `CatalogueItemNamespace` mandatory for action-aware resolution or provide separate type/trait APIs.

`resolve_named_type_entry` converts every domain resolution error—including `AmbiguousIdentifier` and `ClassificationFailed`—to `Ok(None)`. An ambiguous local inherent-impl owner is therefore silently skipped and its method obligations are omitted instead of failing closed with a diagnostic. Match only the explicit external/unresolved case and propagate ambiguity/classification errors.

`resolve_named_type_key` converts `UnresolvedIdentifier` into `Ok(None)`, which the caller silently skips. A missing or misspelled `trait_impls[].for_type` therefore produces no `contract_conformance` obligation while derivation still succeeds. AC-04/CO-04 require unresolved carriers, not only ambiguous ones, to fail closed; propagate a diagnostic instead.

`declaration_identity_in_namespace` derives aliases from the optional raw `module_path` and always adds `crate::Name`. When placement is omitted, this incorrectly treats an unplaced trait as crate-root; when a qualified stored key supplies the module, it fabricates aliases that ignore that module. This can resolve a qualified trait reference to the wrong declaration, contrary to CO-03's exact-placement semantics. Delegate matching to the domain resolver or derive spellings from `FullyQualifiedItemPath` without inventing qualified aliases for unplaced identities.

`catalogue_type_identity_map` collects directly into a `BTreeMap`, so distinct catalogue keys that canonicalize to the same `FullyQualifiedItemPath` silently overwrite each other. For example, `Adapter` with module `alpha` and `domain::alpha::Adapter` both denote the same type identity; `for_type` then resolves to whichever raw key was inserted last instead of failing closed, making the obligation carrier and task-contract attribution arbitrary. Use checked insertion and reject duplicate canonical owners, with regression coverage.
